statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures remain halted since the 21:00 UTC Friday settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in the current hour and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor. Stress eases one point to 55% because a further hour has passed with no verified follow-on step in the US-Iran Hormuz exchange and the IRGC counter-claim is still unconfirmed by CENTCOM. The scheduled 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen now enters the published horizon as its final slot.
recommendation: Tail holds a 4-5% closed-venue floor through the dormant weekend hours and rises gradually to 12% into Sunday evening, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green for the first 23 published hours. The final slot, the scheduled 22:00 UTC reopening hour, is scored at 20% Tail and therefore maps to WATCH and yellow; it is the only published danger window and the first hour in which structure can be scored at all. Stress runs from 55% down to a 52% low and then rebuilds to 70% at the reopen, crossing into the high band in the last three slots. Confidence declines from 85% to 74% as later slots rest on progressively older evidence.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt as the Hormuz tanker exchange stays two-sided and unconfirmed; Sunday's scheduled 22:00 UTC reopen enters the horizon as its single WATCH hour
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September. That reopening hour is now the final slot of this forecast, so for the first time in this weekend sequence the published horizon contains an hour in which a price path can exist.

The macro impulse into the halt is hawkish. August non-farm payrolls printed 162,000 against roughly 56,000 expected with July revised to a 21,000 gain. The 2-year yield rose about 5 basis points to 4.38%, its highest since January 2025, the 10-year added a basis point to 4.776% and the 30-year eased to 5.239%. Rate futures moved to price roughly a 59% probability of a hike at the 15-16 September FOMC, up from about 55% before the release. Equities absorbed that repricing calmly on Friday: the Nasdaq-100 held a small gain and VIX closed at 14.53 inside a 13.80-14.58 range.

The geopolitical sequence is unchanged from the previous assessment and one hour older. US Central Command says American forces struck three Iranian crude oil tankers on Saturday after an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer evaded ballistic missiles fired by the IRGC Navy; the M/T Downy near Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask were permanently disabled and the M/T Kylo was destroyed in the Gulf of Oman. Adm. Brad Cooper framed the action as a tanker-for-tanker economic cost. The IRGC subsequently claimed it had targeted three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels elsewhere, and CENTCOM has not confirmed that counter-claim. No verified follow-on step has been reported in the intervening hour. The campaign is therefore two-sided and unresolved rather than confirmed as an escalation ladder, which is why Stress carries it and Tail does not.

Cross-asset context remains conflicted rather than aligned. WTI is quoted near $91.5 and the complex closed the week up roughly 9%, an oil-led risk premium that pulls against equities. Friday's internals were rotational: semiconductors led firmly while several megacaps fell, and delayed index futures closed split with NQ up 0.14% against ES down 0.42% and YM down 0.57%. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and belong in Stress, not in Tail.

The one substantive change in this assessment is the arrival of the reopening auction inside the horizon. Forty-six hours of accumulated and so far unpriced information, an unresolved military exchange at a shipping chokepoint, an energy premium and untested hawkish rate pricing all meet a single opening auction rather than a continuous session. That concentration is scored as a narrow 20% Tail allowance in the 22:00 UTC slot alone, which maps to WATCH and yellow, and as the only published danger window. It is a conditional gap-and-extension allowance, not an assertion that directional structure has been observed: an orderly two-way auction with genuine retracement would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier of this sequence. Every earlier hour remains at the closed-venue floor and maps to EA_ON. The next 7-day calendar is led by PPI on Thursday 10 September and CPI on Friday 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC that sits beyond this window.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the Friday 21:00 UTC futures settlement and the first twenty-three hours of the CME weekend halt. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from the settlement through 10:00 UTC on 5 September, climbed from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, and rose to 52% by 19:00 UTC and 57% at 20:00 UTC when the Iranian counter-claim was published, easing to 56% through the final two slots as that claim went unconfirmed. Confidence held in a narrow 85-86% band throughout, reflecting a complete evidence set in which only the live price path was unavailable.
outlookSummary: Twenty-three of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with Tail at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing through the dormant middle of the weekend and then rising gradually to 12% into Sunday evening as a gap allowance. The final slot is different: futures are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September, making it the first published hour in which structure can exist. It carries a 20% Tail allowance, maps to WATCH and yellow, and is the only published danger window. Stress opens at 55%, reaches a 52% low in the quietest overnight hours, ticks up from 06:00 UTC as Tel Aviv and Gulf Sunday cash sessions provide the first equity quotes since Friday, and rebuilds to 70% at the reopen, crossing into the high band in the last three slots. The drivers are a two-sided and unconfirmed Hormuz tanker campaign, an oil complex up roughly 9% on the week, and hawkish September rate pricing after the 162K August payroll print, none of which has met an equity quote since Friday. Confidence declines from 85% to 74% because later slots rest on progressively older evidence during an actively developing sequence. Orderly two-way retracement at the reopen would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier.
